description: n=60 CHALLENGE tier (v3.6). Entries are pre-decided by the PI rather than re-screened from x0.8: R201@x0.4 and RC201@x0.5 enter directly. Target band 3-6 instances. Runs THREE arms only, not four -- the n=60 tier exists to show the pipeline still moves at scale, not to carry the main comparison.

admissibility.criterion: CERTIFIED within the work gate, under the v3.6 capped protocol (descent cut at 300,000 LABELS per call with a 120 s non-binding ceiling; certification attempts bounded only by the hard total of 2400+1200=3600 s, at most 3 per run)
admissibility.label_gate_basis: TOTAL labels created in the attempt, including the certification laps
admissibility.why_labels: see n40_cat2_v1: the wall clock drifts 1.68x on bit-identical output
admissibility.provisional: may be adjusted once against the first re-screen batch, with the change recorded in docs/step5-blocker-diagnosis_*.md (the file name carries the latest report timestamp)

truncation_protocol.why: see n40_cat2_v1.protocol.truncation_protocol; the same four defects P1-P4 and the same fixes apply here unchanged

split_rule.statement: Not a split: these entries are directly designated by the PI. Bucket assignment is inherited from n60_cat2_v1 (both are test-bucket instances there as well, each being the cheapest of its family).
split_rule.why: The challenge tier is a scale check, not a matrix; giving it its own bucket rule would imply it carries a train/test comparison it does not carry.
split_rule.probe_source: none -- the probe_* columns below are deliberately ZERO. The 20 s envelope readings are void (they were taken on a degenerate insertion dual under which ~56 of 60 customers had pi ~ 0), and no honest single-call reading exists for these (name, n, tw_scale) triples yet. They are not used for ordering here: with two entries the order is fixed by fiat.
